findings.reason: Only joint action stored is elbow_flexion and the only pattern is elbow_flexion; the raised leg is a balance constraint, not a second working joint.
Description and cues define an isometric hold ('Isometric hold with offset and thick bar loading', 'Maintain a neutral spine throughout the hold'); there are no repetitions to count.
Static hold of maximum heel elevation; sibling paused_isometric_calf_raise_hold is stored as time.

The kettlebells are handles, not load; nothing external is lifted. Siblings plyo_push_up and clap_push_up are bodyweight_reps, and the stored comparison_scope is already bodyweight_aware, which contradicts weight_reps/total_load.
No external load anywhere in the description or equipment (stability ball only); load_input_mode total_load has nothing to record.
Isometric balance on the glutes and hands supporting only body mass; the comparable l_sit is stored bodyweight=true.
Load is read off one specific lever gripper machine's stack/lever ratio, so the number is not comparable across gyms; every other cam/lever machine in the sample uses equipment_instance.

The posterior deltoid is the stated target and is stored primary, yet it carries the lowest tension profile in the row while the secondary trapezius_middle is moderate/high/high - the target cannot be the least loaded muscle in a horizontal abduction.
The lift starts from a dead stop on pins at chest height, i.e. the fully lengthened pec position under full load; tension_lengthened 'low' contradicts the defining feature of the movement.
The bar starts at knee height, so the hip extensors never reach the lengthened position a floor deadlift reaches; the profile is identical to hook_grip_deadlift despite the truncated bottom range.

non_vocabulary_findings.problem: Equipment is stored as pull_up_bar + dip_bars, but the execution cues are 'Sit with hands placed on the floor behind your hips' - a floor V-sit needs no equipment.
Equipment is stored as 'barbell' while the description and cues describe a seated lever gripper machine ('Adjust the seat height and grip the handles').

Equipment is stored as 'barbell' although resistance_source is cam_machine and the exercise is a lever machine shrug; additionally forearm_flexors are listed as a secondary mover on a shrug whose entire point is that no manual grip is used.
latissimus_dorsi is stored as a secondary mover of an overhead press. The lat is a shoulder extensor/adductor, i.e. the antagonist of the pressing action.
Same contradiction: latissimus_dorsi stored as secondary mover in an overhead press, where it is the antagonist.

Stored as wrist_extension with forearm_extensors primary. A 'back' (behind-the-back) wrist curl is wrist flexion driven by the forearm flexors - the catalogue's own behind_the_back_wrist_curl and cable_standing_back_wrist_curl are stored as wrist_flexion / forearm_flexors.

Description says the reverse preacher curl is done 'using an underhand grip'. A reverse curl is by definition pronated (overhand); the stored muscle profile (biceps_brachii_long primary, brachialis/brachioradialis secondary) also matches a supinated curl rather than a reverse curl.

erector_spinae is stored primary with high lengthened/midrange tension, but the described action is tilting the pelvis to flatten the lower back (posterior tilt), which is produced by the abdominals and glutes while the erectors lengthen and release.
